question: Should this fix invalidate every affected provider and Pi cost-cache artifact on upgrade, accepting one full rescan to eliminate stale persisted offsets?
rationale: The scanner fix is narrow, but the cross-provider artifact-version bump intentionally changes upgrade behavior and its one-time CPU and I/O cost requires area-owner acceptance.

options.title: Accept one-time rebuild
options.body: Keep the version bumps and require live upgrade proof showing caches rebuild correctly and subsequent scans return to incremental behavior.

options.title: Narrow invalidation
options.body: Revise the migration to preserve compatible cached totals while clearing only offsets that may have consumed an incomplete tail.

recommendation.title: Accept one-time rebuild
recommendation.body: Keep the version bumps and require live upgrade proof showing caches rebuild correctly and subsequent scans return to incremental behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest history signal for the JSONL scanner's incremental performance behavior.
